scenes.title: Twelve ships leave Troy
scenes.caption: Odysseus tells the whole voyage himself, years later, at the court of the Phaeacian king Alcinous. He begins it here, with the wind that carried him from Troy. (Book 9)

scenes.title: Maron’s gift
scenes.caption: At Ismarus, Odysseus spares Maron, a priest of Apollo, and his family. Maron gives him gold, a silver bowl and twelve jars of strong wine—the wine he later takes into the Cyclops’s cave. (Book 9)

scenes.title: The cost of staying
scenes.caption: Odysseus urges an immediate departure, but his men stay to feast on the shore. The Cicones return with reinforcements and drive them back to sea; six men from each ship are lost. (Book 9)

scenes.title: Blown past Cape Malea
scenes.caption: Off Cape Malea, the north wind and current push the fleet away from its course to Ithaca. For nine days the ships are driven across unfamiliar water before reaching the Lotus-eaters. (Book 9)

scenes.title: Food that makes them stay
scenes.caption: The Lotus-eaters welcome the three scouts and share their food. Those who taste it no longer want to report back or return home; they want to remain and eat lotus. (Book 9)

scenes.title: Back beneath the benches
scenes.caption: Odysseus brings the reluctant scouts back by force and secures them beneath the rowing benches. He orders everyone else aboard before they too can taste the lotus. (Book 9)

scenes.title: Inside the shepherd’s cave
scenes.caption: The cave holds racks of cheese, pens of lambs and kids, and vessels full of whey. The companions want to take supplies and leave, but Odysseus waits to meet the owner. (Book 9)

scenes.title: The name Nobody
scenes.caption: Odysseus calls himself Nobody and gives Polyphemus Maron’s wine. When the giant sleeps, the men blind his single eye with a sharpened stake; his neighbours hear that Nobody is hurting him. (Book 9)

scenes.title: Out beneath the ram
scenes.caption: At dawn, Polyphemus feels the sheep’s backs as they leave. Odysseus escapes beneath the largest ram, but later shouts his real name from the ship. The Cyclops calls on his father Poseidon to punish him. (Book 9)

scenes.title: Aeolus’s island
scenes.caption: Aeolus lives on an island enclosed by a metal wall above a sheer rock face. He welcomes Odysseus for a month and asks him about Troy and the returning Greek fleet. (Book 10)

scenes.title: The sealed oxhide bag
scenes.caption: Before they leave, Aeolus shuts the troublesome winds in an oxhide bag and ties it with a silver cord. Only the west wind remains free to carry the ships toward Ithaca. (Book 10)

scenes.title: Fires on the home shore
scenes.caption: On the tenth day, Ithaca comes into view, close enough for the crew to see fires ashore. Odysseus, exhausted from steering without rest, finally falls asleep. (Book 10)

scenes.title: They open the bag
scenes.caption: They are so close that they can see men tending fires on the shore. When the winds carry them back, Aeolus drives them away as men the gods must hate. (Book 10)

scenes.title: A second request refused
scenes.caption: Odysseus returns with a herald and a companion to ask for help. Aeolus sends him away, convinced that a man so unlucky must be hated by the gods. (Book 10)

scenes.title: The harbour before the attack
scenes.caption: The fleet enters a narrow harbour enclosed by steep cliffs and moors close together in the still water. Odysseus keeps his own ship outside, tied to a rock at the entrance. (Book 10)

scenes.title: Only one ship gets away
scenes.caption: The Laestrygonians hurl rocks from the cliffs and destroy the ships inside the harbour. Odysseus cuts his mooring cable and orders his rowers out to sea; the rest of the fleet is lost. (Book 10)

scenes.title: Animals outside Circe’s house
scenes.caption: In a forest clearing, the scouts find Circe’s stone house. Wolves and lions approach them without attacking, and from inside they hear her singing as she works at her loom. (Book 10)

scenes.title: The herb Hermes gives him
scenes.caption: Hermes meets Odysseus on the way to Circe’s house and gives him moly. Homer describes a black root and a milk-white flower; the herb protects him from Circe’s drug. (Book 10)

scenes.title: The companions restored
scenes.caption: Circe’s drink and wand turn the men into pigs, though their minds remain human. After Odysseus resists her magic, she restores them; they stay on Aeaea for a year before asking to leave. (Book 10)

scenes.title: A shore without sunlight
scenes.caption: The ship reaches the land of the Cimmerians beside Ocean. Mist and darkness cover the shore; the crew beaches the vessel and follows the water to the place Circe described. (Book 11)

scenes.title: Tiresias’s warning
scenes.caption: Tiresias warns Odysseus to leave the Sun’s cattle unharmed. If the crew kills them, their ship and lives will be lost; Odysseus may still reach home, but late and alone. (Book 11)

scenes.title: His mother’s shade
scenes.caption: Anticlea tells him that Penelope is still waiting and that grief for her absent son ended her own life. Three times Odysseus tries to embrace her; three times the shade slips through his arms. (Book 11)

scenes.title: Elpenor’s oar
scenes.caption: Back on Aeaea, the crew burns Elpenor’s body and armour, raises a burial mound, and plants his oar above it. They fulfil the request he made when they met his shade. (Book 12)

scenes.title: Instructions for the next passage
scenes.caption: While the crew sleeps beside the ship, Circe tells Odysseus about the Sirens, the two dangerous rocks and the Sun’s herds. She urges him to pass Scylla quickly instead of trying to fight her. (Book 12)

scenes.title: Wax for the rowers
scenes.caption: As the wind drops, the men stow the sail and take up their oars. Odysseus cuts and kneads wax for their ears, then has himself bound to the mast so he alone can hear the Sirens. (Book 12)

scenes.title: Rowing past the singers
scenes.caption: The Sirens offer Odysseus knowledge of Troy and the world. He signals to be released, but the crew tightens his bonds and rows on until the voices can no longer be heard. (Book 12)

scenes.title: Water drawn into Charybdis
scenes.caption: Charybdis draws the sea down beneath a low rock with a fig tree above it. Odysseus orders the helmsman away from the whirlpool and tells the frightened men to keep rowing. (Book 12)

scenes.title: The danger above them
scenes.caption: While the men watch Charybdis, Scylla reaches down from her high cave and takes six of them. The ship escapes, but the loss follows Odysseus long after they leave the strait. (Book 12)

scenes.place: Thrinacia — the cattle of the Sun
scenes.title: The cattle of the Sun
scenes.caption: On Thrinacia, the cattle and sheep belong to Helios. Odysseus repeats the warning and makes his men swear to leave the herds alone, eating only the provisions aboard their ship. (Book 12)

scenes.place: Thrinacia — the cattle of the Sun
scenes.title: A month of contrary winds
scenes.caption: Contrary winds keep them on the island for a month. When the food runs out, the men catch fish and birds; while Odysseus sleeps inland, Eurylochus persuades them to kill the sacred cattle. (Book 12)

scenes.place: Thrinacia — the cattle of the Sun
scenes.title: Mast and keel
scenes.caption: After they sail again, Zeus strikes the ship with lightning. Odysseus lashes the mast and keel together and survives alone; the current carries him back past Charybdis before he reaches Calypso’s island. (Book 12)

scenes.title: The cave and its four springs
scenes.caption: Around Calypso’s cave grow alder, poplar, cypress and a grapevine; four streams water the meadows. Odysseus spends seven years on the island, still longing for Ithaca despite her offer of immortality. (Books 5, 7)

scenes.title: Making the raft
scenes.caption: Ordered to release him, Calypso provides tools and sailcloth. Odysseus cuts twenty trees, shapes and joins the timbers, and adds a deck, mast, steering oar and wicker sides; he finishes in four days. (Book 5)

scenes.title: Steering by the stars
scenes.caption: At sea, Odysseus watches the Pleiades, Boötes and the Bear. Following Calypso’s instructions, he keeps the Bear on his left; on the eighteenth day he sees the mountains of Scheria. (Book 5)

scenes.title: Shelter under the olives
scenes.caption: Poseidon’s storm destroys the raft. After reaching a river mouth, Odysseus finds two intertwined olive bushes and covers himself with fallen leaves, hiding from the cold until morning. (Book 5)

scenes.title: Nausicaa at the washing pools
scenes.caption: Nausicaa and her attendants wash clothes by the river and then play ball. Their cries wake Odysseus; Nausicaa stays when the others run and arranges food, clothing and directions to the city. (Book 6)

scenes.title: Fruit through every season
scenes.caption: Outside Alcinous’s palace, pears, apples, pomegranates, figs and olives grow in a walled garden. Homer describes fruit ripening throughout the year, with streams watering the orchard and supplying the town. (Book 7)

scenes.title: The story behind his tears
scenes.caption: When Demodocus sings about Troy, Odysseus hides his tears beneath his cloak. Alcinous notices and asks who he is; at last he gives his name and tells the Phaeacians about his wanderings. (Books 8–9)

scenes.title: Home while he sleeps
scenes.caption: The Phaeacians carry Odysseus to Ithaca asleep and lay him on the sand with his gifts nearby. When he wakes, Athena’s mist prevents him from recognising the harbour at first. (Book 13)

scenes.title: Argos recognises him
scenes.caption: Disguised as a beggar, Odysseus reaches his house with Eumaeus. His old dog Argos recognises him, lowers his ears and wags his tail, but can no longer rise; Odysseus turns aside to hide a tear. (Book 17)

scenes.title: The bow in his hands
scenes.caption: The suitors fail to string Odysseus’s bow. Still dressed as a beggar, he examines it and strings it easily, then sends an arrow through the twelve axes; the contest turns into the struggle to reclaim his house. (Books 21–22)

scenes.title: The bed that cannot be moved
scenes.caption: After the suitors are defeated, Penelope tests him by asking for their bed to be moved. Odysseus explains that he built it around a rooted olive trunk, trimmed into a bedpost. She recognises the secret they share. (Book 23)
